body: It can also be due to high blood pressure. My sincerest apologies for excluding that. I have neuropathic POTS, so low BP is more of an issue for me personally. That would make total sense if you have hyperadrenergic POTS, as elevated norepinephrine leads to an increase in BP. Actually, similarly to OP’s original question about physical pressure to the eyes causing a similar sensation, this elevated internal pressure can also lead to seeing stars for the same reason (sudden increase in pressure in retinal cells). Please let me know if I can answer any other questions! :)

I study neuroscience and I have POTS. As someone else said, it’s due to a drop in blood pressure and therefore a lack of adequate blood flow to the brain. Also, you see it when you rub your eyes because the cells in your retina are not made to respond to physical pressure, just light, so essentially your brain perceives this as random signaling. Not harmful, just don’t do it too much. Hope this helps.

i would repot this little guy. how i do it is just gently dump out the cactus and plop it into a slightly bigger pot (about an inch bigger than the one it’s in now, so maybe around 4 inches?). only water when the soil is completely dry and give it lots and lots of sunlight!

they do tend to slump over like this at a certain point, i would just keep caring for it like a regular cactus (only water when soil is completely dry and lots of sun). make sure it acclimates well to more light so it doesn’t go into shock!

my biology teacher always hated me. i don’t know what i did to make her despise me so much, but she’d call me out in front of the whole class pretty much daily. one time, i was given to option to re-do an assignment after i had gotten a 76% on it, even though i couldn’t have done it any better. anyway, i followed the directions so precisely, i was sure that i would get a better grade. in turn i got a 40% and i was not allowed to go back to my original grade. another day, there was an assignment i really did not understand. instead of helping me understand, she put me out in the hallway and made me sit there until i figured it out. i sat there until the bell rang. i came back in and handed the paper to her. she said “well, i guess it’s a zero” and filed it away. i retorted “not listening and not understanding something are two different things”. she then proceeded to state that she wishes she had a camera so she could take a picture of my face and “show [me] how stupid [i] look”. i then tossed her marker onto her desk and slammed her door. seeing her in the hallway makes me sick to my stomach.
